entries.clue: Turn aside first signs of demands emerging from lecturer (7)

indicatorNotes.first signs of: the first sign of a word is its opening letter
indicatorNotes.emerging from: the letters come out of the front of the word that follows

blocks.note: the opening letters of demands, emerging and from
LECT sits at the start of lecturer

annotation.surface: A lecturer keeps making demands, and a student tries to deflect them.
annotation.walkthrough: The first-letters rule runs across three words, 'demands emerging from', before the last word supplies its own opening four letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shield deflects a blow by turning it aside, and you deflect a demand the same way.

entries.clue: Equestrian competitor still on terrace (7)

blocks.note: Ter. is the street-name abbreviation for Terrace

annotation.surface: A horse rider waits motionless on a terrace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as motionless, but it is the intensifier in 'still better' = 'even better'. An eventer competes in horse trials: dressage, cross-country and jumping.
annotation.definitionFit: An eventer is a rider who competes in eventing, a horse-trials competition.

entries.clue: Early form of insect found in similar valleys (5)

indicatorNotes.found in: the answer is found inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A naturalist finds the same insect in several comparable valleys.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the word break between 'similar' and 'valleys'.
annotation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature stage of an insect, before the pupa.

entries.clue: Funny doctor following beginners in children’s orthopaedics (7)

indicatorNotes.beginners in: the beginners of words are their first letters
indicatorNotes.following: MEDIC comes after the first letters

blocks.note: first letters of children's and orthopaedics

annotation.surface: A doctor on a children's bone ward has a sense of humour.
annotation.walkthrough: Blocks run in answer order: 'following' puts the doctor after the two initials.
annotation.definitionFit: Comedic means relating to comedy, so funny.

entries.clue: Ordinary fellow is fed rubbish creating infringement on a field (7)

indicatorNotes.rubbish: as an adjective, rubbish means badly made, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: O = ordinary, as in O level

annotation.surface: An ordinary man is fed junk food and commits a foul on the pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fed rubbish' reads as a poor diet; 'rubbish' is actually the instruction to jumble IS FED.
annotation.definitionFit: Offside is an infringement in football, rugby and hockey, all played on a field.

entries.clue: Facilities in France, Germany and Sweden for natural disasters? (6)

indicatorNotes.in: LOO goes inside the country letters

blocks.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
D and S are the vehicle codes for Germany and Sweden

annotation.surface: European countries prepare emergency facilities against natural disasters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facilities' sounds like emergency infrastructure, but it is the euphemism for toilets. Loo is British for toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: floods are one kind of natural disaster, like earthquakes or droughts.

entries.clue: Place sect transformed in striking display (9)

indicatorNotes.transformed: the letters are changed into a new form

annotation.surface: A religious sect is converted during some dramatic ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a verb telling you where to put something; it is just five letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fireworks or a pageant put on to be looked at make a spectacle.

entries.clue: Dorothy shortly facing bank gets more eccentric (7)

indicatorNotes.shortly: use the short form of the name
indicatorNotes.facing: DOT sits in front of TIER

blocks.note: Dot is a pet form of Dorothy
a bank = a tier, a row, as in a bank of seats

annotation.surface: Dorothy, confronting her bank manager, is growing more peculiar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money or a river; here it is a row or level, like a bank of seats or keys.
annotation.definitionFit: Dotty means mildly crazy, so dottier is more eccentric.

entries.clue: Starting point altered for pastime near to tracks? (13)

annotation.surface: Someone moves the starting line of a hobby that happens beside the railway.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: trainspotting, the British hobby of logging locomotive numbers, is done beside railway tracks.
annotation.definitionFit: Trainspotting is a hobby carried out at the trackside, watching trains.

entries.clue: Try, in this place, to be heard (4)

blocks.clueFragment: in this place, to be heard
blocks.note: the one-word adverb for 'in this place', spoken rather than spelt, as the last three words ask

annotation.surface: A court insists that a case be tried here so it gets a hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the courtroom sense: a judge hears a case. Read as 'attempt' it goes nowhere.
annotation.definitionFit: A judge who tries a case hears it.

entries.clue: Trainee Tom misplaced thing worked on strings (10)

indicatorNotes.misplaced: the letters are put in the wrong places

annotation.surface: A trainee called Tom loses something he was working on with strings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worked' reads as labour; for a puppet it means operated.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the string puppet is described by how it is operated rather than named.

entries.clue: Thin thread in piece of furniture for displaying things? About right (6)

indicatorNotes.About: the furniture goes about, around, the R

blocks.clueFragment: piece of furniture for displaying things?
blocks.note: a stand displays goods or ornaments

annotation.surface: A thin thread is caught on a display cabinet.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the furniture is defined loosely, by what it does. 'About right' reads as 'roughly correct' but splits into a container instruction and a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a single fibre of hair, rope or yarn is a strand.

entries.clue: Denial? It requires breakdown from top to bottom (2,6)

indicatorNotes.breakdown: the words are broken down and rebuilt

annotation.surface: Getting past denial takes a total psychological breakdown.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and full stop break the fodder across two sentences; 'Denial' and 'It' join as one set of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Examining something from top to bottom is going through it in detail.

entries.clue: Container for documents in short-lived legal event (9)

annotation.surface: A lawyer's papers go in a bag during a quick court hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: A barrister's instructions are also called a brief, which makes the legal surface fit the answer twice over.
annotation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat case for carrying documents.

entries.clue: A German among five bridge players showing enthusiasm (9)

indicatorNotes.among: A GER is placed among the bridge letters

blocks.note: bridge players sit at N, S, E, W; five of them here are E, N, E, S, S

annotation.surface: A German joins a card table of five and shows great keenness.
annotation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named for compass points, so any string of N, S, E and W is available; here five of them surround the German.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name the keen wish to get on with something.

entries.clue: Frightening evidence of injury shown by unknown character (5)

blocks.note: a scar shows an old injury
x, y and z are the unknowns in algebra

annotation.surface: A menacing stranger bears a nasty scar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unknown character' sounds like a mysterious stranger; in crosswords it is an algebra letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, scary being the informal word: a scary film is a frightening one.

entries.clue: Item put on floor kept by daughter and son for forms of medication (5)

indicatorNotes.kept by: RUG is held between D and S

blocks.note: a rug is laid on the floor

annotation.surface: A family keeps medicines under a rug.
annotation.walkthrough: D(RUG)S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the medical sense: pills and injections a doctor prescribes are drugs.

entries.clue: Set free concerning rental agreement (7)

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in memo headers
a lease is a rental agreement

annotation.surface: A tenant is let out of a rental contract.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a tenant being freed from a lease, while 'free' is the definition and 'concerning' supplies RE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prisoners and hostages are released, set free.

entries.clue: Trick by Eric upset, say, retired hotel employee (9)

indicatorNotes.upset: ERIC is knocked over and rearranged
indicatorNotes.retired: EG goes back, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: say = e.g., for example, turned back

annotation.surface: Eric is upset by a trick played on him by a retired hotel worker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the usual crossword cue for EG, 'for example'. 'Retired' reads as someone's pension but means going backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A concierge is the hotel employee who helps guests with bookings and errands.

entries.clue: Children with a sign of amusement – or annoyance? (7)

annotation.surface: Do children make you smile or make you cross?
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay spells 'a grin', amusement, while the definition is its opposite, which the question mark enjoys.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though chagrin is specifically the vexation of being disappointed or shown up.

entries.clue: Good artist given praise after turn is unhurried (7)

indicatorNotes.after: the praise comes after G and RA
indicatorNotes.turn: to turn something is to rotate it, so the word faces the other way and reads backwards

annotation.surface: A fine painter wins praise after a slow, patient performance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a stage act; it is the instruction to reverse LAUD.
annotation.definitionFit: Something gradual happens slowly, without hurry.

entries.clue: Make certain English nurse is prepared (6)

indicatorNotes.is prepared: NURSE is made ready, rearranged into a new form

annotation.surface: An English nurse double-checks she is ready for her shift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' in the sense of dressed or made up, as a dish is prepared, tells you to rework NURSE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ensuring the door is locked is making certain of it.

entries.clue: Musical instrument wrongly let in car (8)

indicatorNotes.wrongly: the letters are put in the wrong order

annotation.surface: Someone lets a musical instrument into a car when they should not.
annotation.walkthrough: A short all-in-one-line anagram: definition first, then the indicator, then the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the clarinet is one example of a musical instrument, a single-reed woodwind.

entries.clue: A secondary thoroughfare overseas? (6)

blocks.note: British roads are graded by letter, the lesser grade coming second after the main roads

annotation.surface: Looking for a minor road in a foreign country.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain main roads are A roads and lesser ones B roads, so a secondary road is 'a B road', which runs together as ABROAD.
annotation.definitionFit: Abroad means overseas, in a foreign country.

entries.clue: Some mature captain’s summary (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters that follow are used

annotation.surface: An experienced ship's captain gives a briefing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Captain's summary' looks like a single phrase, but the definition is just 'summary'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, recap being the everyday clipping of recapitulation, a restatement of the main points.

entries.clue: Urge parent developed to get exciting book (4-6)

indicatorNotes.developed: the letters are worked into something new

annotation.surface: A child pesters a parent into buying a gripping book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Urge' reads as a verb commanding the reader; it is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a book so exciting you keep turning the pages.

entries.clue: Firm linked to leading masterstroke (4)

indicatorNotes.linked to: CO is joined directly to UP

blocks.note: up = ahead, leading, as in 'two goals up'

annotation.surface: A company tied to the market leader pulls off a brilliant move.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Firm' can be an adjective, meaning solid; here it is a business.
annotation.definitionFit: A coup is a brilliantly successful stroke or move.

entries.clue: Fine point before journalist dined sumptuously (7)

indicatorNotes.before: the pieces come in front of ED

blocks.note: F = fine, as on pencil leads

annotation.surface: A journalist, just before making a fine point, has eaten lavishly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine point' reads as a subtle argument; it splits into F and a compass point.
annotation.definitionFit: To feast is to eat a large, rich meal.

entries.clue: At home awkward type grips line in a clumsy way (7)

indicatorNotes.awkward: TYPE is put in an awkward order
indicatorNotes.grips: whatever grips something holds it tight inside, so the jumbled letters close around L

annotation.surface: An awkward person at home clutches a rope clumsily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Awkward type' reads as a clumsy person, echoing the definition; 'awkward' is really the anagram cue for TYPE, which then wraps L: EPT(L)Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Ineptly means without skill, in a clumsy way.
